feedback.problem: The mass density function $\lambda $ of a rectangular flat plate that occupies the region $D={(x,y)\,:\,0\le x\le 1,\,0\le y\le 2}$ is given by $\lambda (x,y)=y{e}^{xy}.$ What is the total mass of the plate?
feedback.worked_solution:
The mass $M$ of a plate that occupies the region $D={(x,y)\,:\,0\le x\le 1,\,0\le y\le 2}$ with mass density $\lambda (x,y)=y{e}^{xy}$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ={∬}_{D}y{e}^{xy}\,\text{d}A.\end{aligned}
$$

First, we express our double integral as a repeated integral:      

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}y{e}^{xy}\,\text{d}A & ={\int }_{0}^{2}[{\int }_{0}^{1}y{e}^{xy}\,\text{d}x]\text{d}y\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we evaluate the inner integral by integrating with respect to $x$, treating $y$ as a constant:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{2}[{\int }_{0}^{1}y{e}^{xy}\,\text{d}x]\text{d}y & ={\int }_{0}^{2}y[{\int }_{0}^{1}{e}^{xy}\,\text{d}x]\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}[{e}^{xy}]_{0}^{1}\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}({e}^{y}-{e}^{0})\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}({e}^{y}-1)\,\text{d}y\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we integrate with respect to $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{2}({e}^{y}-1)\,\text{d}y & =[{e}^{y}-y]_{0}^{2} \\  & =({e}^{2}-2)-(1-0) \\  & ={e}^{2}-3\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the mass of the plate is $M={e}^{2}-3.$
